blocks.title: We start with a walk, not a drawing
blocks.text:
Before a line is drawn we visit the site, or the room, at different times of day. We note where the light lands, where the wind comes from and how people already move through the space.

Then we make models, samples and plenty of sketches, so you can judge ideas with your hands and not only on screen.

blocks.text:
We design with pencils, card models and real samples before we open any software. It slows the first weeks down and speeds everything after.

We work closely with a small group of builders, joiners and landscape designers. They join the conversation early, which keeps drawings honest and costs predictable.

projects.title: Linden House
projects.summary: A two-storey family house with a timber garden room that opens onto an orchard.
projects.story:
The clients wanted a house that felt connected to the garden in every season. We placed the living spaces on the south side, behind tall windows, and gave the kitchen a low timber island where the whole family gathers.

The walls are lime render and the garden room is clad in larch, which will silver with time. Inside, a green sofa and long bookshelves give the living room its character.

projects.title: Kiln Street Apartment
projects.summary: A city flat with deep teal walls, warm timber and one big orange sofa.
projects.story:
A small apartment in a converted pottery. The owners love colour, so we painted the main room a deep teal and let a burnt orange sofa carry the room.

The galley kitchen is fitted in dark green with brass handles, and the bedroom is kept calm with timber, linen and soft bedside light.

projects.title: The Reading Room
projects.summary: A public reading room with long tables, green lamps and walls of books.
projects.story:
A neighbourhood library moved into a former warehouse and asked for a room people would want to stay in. We built a double-height wall of shelving, long oak tables and a row of green reading lamps.

The window seat at the far end is the most requested spot in the building.

projects.title: Ember & Oat
projects.summary: A neighbourhood café with a terracotta counter, striped awning and a green banquette.
projects.story:
The owners wanted a warm, unfussy café that works for a quick coffee and a long lunch. A terracotta-tiled counter anchors the room, and the green banquette runs along the window so every table has daylight.

Outside, a striped awning and pavement tables give the corner a friendly face.

projects.title: Brightline Works
projects.summary: A glazed office building with a deep roof and an open-plan floor full of daylight.
projects.story:
A design company needed an office where everyone sits near a window. A deep roof shades the glazed upper floor, and a concrete band below gives the building weight.

Inside, rows of white desks run parallel to the façade and a quiet library room sits at the centre of the plan.

projects.title: Maple Row Kitchen
projects.summary: A dark, tired kitchen opened up with sage cabinets, an oak floor and a family island.
projects.story:
The old kitchen had dark cabinets, ochre walls and tiles that had seen better days. We removed one wall, replaced the floor with oak and fitted sage green cabinets with a timber island.

Two pendant lights hang over the island, which is now where homework, cooking and conversation happen at once.

pairs.caption: The kitchen before and after the work

projects.title: Pearl Bathroom
projects.summary: A beige bathroom turned into a calm green room with a timber vanity.
projects.story:
The clients disliked their cold, beige bathroom. We kept the layout, which worked well, and changed everything you see: green tiles to shoulder height, a timber vanity with a round basin and a brass-framed mirror.

The window stays unfrosted and looks out over the garden.

gallery.caption: Timber vanity with a round basin

pairs.caption: The bathroom before and after the work

projects.title: Orchard Cottage
projects.summary: A small brick cottage gains a glazed timber extension facing the orchard.
projects.story:
The cottage was charming but dark, with a lean-to shed at the back. We replaced the shed with a glazed timber extension that holds a kitchen and dining room facing the orchard.

The new roof is a different shape from the old one on purpose, so the extension reads as a new chapter in the cottage’s story.

gallery.caption: The extension seen from the garden

pairs.caption: The cottage before and after the extension

projects.title: Saltmarsh Cabin
projects.summary: A dark timber cabin raised on posts above the marsh, lined in pine inside.
projects.story:
A weekend cabin for two on a flood-prone marsh edge. The building stands on posts so water can pass beneath, and its dark timber skin blends with the reeds.

Inside, pine lines every surface, a wood stove warms the main room and a single large window frames the water.

services.summary: New houses and small buildings, designed around light, place and the way you live.
services.text: We design new homes and small buildings from the first site visit to the final inspection. We handle planning applications, technical drawings and the tender, and we visit the site through construction.

services.title: Interior design
services.summary: Layouts, joinery, colour, lighting and furniture, designed together as one room.
services.text: Whether it is one room or a whole home, we design the layout, the joinery and the details together, so nothing feels added afterwards. We provide samples you can handle before you decide.

services.title: Renovation and extensions
services.summary: New life for kitchens, bathrooms and older houses, with extensions that respect what is there.
services.text: Older buildings reward patience. We survey carefully, keep what works and add only what the building needs. We have renovated kitchens, bathrooms, cottages and townhouses.

services.title: Cafés, offices and public rooms
services.summary: Welcoming rooms for customers, colleagues and neighbours, designed to work hard every day.
services.text: We design cafés, offices and community spaces where daily use matters as much as looks. We plan circulation, acoustics and daylight with the people who will run the space.

journal.title: Why we start every project with a walk
journal.summary: Before any drawing, we visit the site at three different times of day. Here is what we look for.
journal.body:
The first thing we do on a new project is visit. Not for an hour, but for most of a day, and sometimes again in the evening.

We look for where the light lands in the morning and where it lingers in the afternoon. We note where the wind comes from, which neighbours can see in and which views are worth keeping.

We also watch how people already move. In a house, that might be where the family drops its bags. In a café, it is where the queue forms.

These notes end up as the first page of every project file, and we return to them whenever a decision gets difficult.

journal.title: Five materials, one room: how we choose a palette
journal.summary: Oak, stone, terracotta, brass and tile: a quick guide to making a palette that feels calm.
journal.body:
A good palette is smaller than you think. We rarely use more than five materials in a room.

We start with one natural material that will age well, such as oak or stone. Then we add one colour that carries the room, like terracotta or deep green, and one metal for the details.

Samples live on a table in our material library. We ask clients to take them home and look at them in their own light, at different times of day, before anything is ordered.

journal.title: A timber frame goes up at Saltmarsh
journal.summary: The frame of the cabin was raised in two days. A few photos and notes from the site.
journal.body:
The Saltmarsh frame arrived in numbered pieces and went up in two days with a crew of five.

Because the building stands on posts, the first job was setting the posts to millimetre accuracy. Everything else followed from that.

We visit weekly, but the frame raising is the day we never miss.

journal.title: Ember & Oat, one year on
journal.summary: We went back to the café at dusk to see how the room is used.
journal.body:
We went back to Ember & Oat on a Friday evening. The banquette was full, the pendant lights were glowing and the pavement tables were taken.

What made us happiest was that the staff had moved nothing. The counter, the stools and the tables are exactly where we drew them.
